{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLVQezAJGSsW9LM1jkTi","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01LrshSzpSPuBtMMtfwdwFoD","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-003/2026-07-24T073017Z-claude-no-skill-3/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Review: Stake Widget\n\n```jsx\nconst [hasApproved, setHasApproved] = useState(false);\n\n{isConnected && (\n  <div>\n    {!hasApproved && (\n      <button onClick={async () => { await approve(); setHasApproved(true); }}>\n        Approve\n      </button>\n    )}\n    <button onClick={stake}>Stake</button>\n  </div>\n)}\n```\n\n## 1. Wrong-network user (Arbitrum, mainnet-only app, zero allowance)\n\nThe only gate on rendering is `isConnected`. `isConnected` is true whenever a\nwallet is attached — it says nothing about **which chain** the wallet is on. So:\n\n- **The widget renders in full.** `hasApproved` is `false`, so the **Approve**\n  button shows; **Stake** always shows. The user sees both buttons and no hint\n  that they're on the wrong network.\n- **Click Approve** → `approve()` sends a write to the token's mainnet address,\n  but the wallet is pointed at Arbitrum. Best case the wallet rejects / the call\n  reverts (no such contract, or a *different* contract at that address). Then\n  `setHasApproved(true)` does **not** run (the `await` throws), so at least the\n  button stays. Worst case the address happens to hold an unrelated contract and\n  the tx does something unintended.\n- **Click Stake** → same story: a write against the mainnet stake contract while\n  connected to Arbitrum. Reverts or hits the wrong address.\n\n**Missing:** a network guard. Nothing checks `chainId === mainnet.id`, so the\nuser can burn gas / sign against the wrong chain with zero feedback.\n\n## 2. The subtler bug: `hasApproved` shows a button that can't work\n\n`hasApproved` is **local component state**, not on-chain truth. It goes `true`\nonce, optimistically, the moment `approve()` resolves, and stays `true`. It is\nnever reconciled with the actual allowance. That makes it lie.\n\n**Concrete sequence (account switch — persistent dead end):**\n\n1. Connect account **A** (allowance 0). Approve button + Stake button show.\n2. Click **Approve**, approval confirms, `setHasApproved(true)`. Now only\n   **Stake** shows — correct for A.\n3. In the wallet, switch to account **B** (allowance 0). The component does\n   **not** remount, so `hasApproved` stays `true`.\n4. **Result:** Approve is hidden (because `hasApproved`), only Stake shows — but\n   B has zero allowance, so **Stake reverts and there is no way to approve.**\n   The one visible button cannot work.\n\n**Second sequence (optimistic-set race, same session):**\n\n1. Click **Approve**. `approve()` resolves as soon as the tx is *submitted*, so\n   `setHasApproved(true)` runs before the allowance actually lands on chain.\n2. Immediately click **Stake** (before the approval tx mines). Allowance is\n   still 0 → **Stake reverts**, and Approve is already hidden.\n\n(Related: if approval is for the exact stake amount, a successful stake consumes\nit back to 0, but `hasApproved` stays `true` — the next stake shows an\nun-workable Stake button and no Approve.)\n\nRoot cause in one line: **approval is derived from \"did I click approve this\nsession\" instead of \"what is the allowance right now.\"**\n\n## 3. The flow this widget should implement\n\n**Approval status must come from the chain**, not `useState`. Read the token's\n`allowance(owner = connected address, spender = stake contract)` with wagmi's\n`useReadContract`, keyed on `{ address, chainId, spender, amount }`. Refetch on\naccount change, chain change, and after the approve receipt confirms\n(`useWaitForTransactionReceipt`). Compare `allowance >= stakeAmount`. Local state\nis fine only for pending/loading UI, never as the source of truth.\n\n**Render exactly one primary action.** Evaluate the checks in this priority\norder and stop at the first that fails:\n\n1. **Not connected** → `Connect Wallet`.\n2. **Wrong network** (`chainId !== mainnet.id`) → `Switch to Mainnet`\n   (`switchChain`). Block everything below.\n3. **Invalid input / insufficient balance** (amount empty or `> balance`) →\n   disabled `Stake` with reason, or a validation prompt.\n4. **`allowance < stakeAmount`** → `Approve`. After it confirms, refetch\n   allowance (which flips this check), don't guess.\n5. **Otherwise** → `Stake`.\n\n**One button at a time.** Approve and Stake should never be visible together —\nStake only appears once the on-chain allowance actually covers the amount. While\nany tx is in flight, show that single button in a disabled/loading state.\n\nThis removes both bugs: the network check stops wrong-chain writes, and sourcing\napproval from the live allowance means switching accounts, a dropped approval, or\na consumed allowance all correctly bring the **Approve** button back.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5898,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5898},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"eb1255fc-7894-4c36-9c39-e6c5e25f344a","uuid":"a0a87b7a-c728-4b92-b361-2a07462ed6c6","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:31:15.728Z","request_id":"req_011CdLVQcNtwto1HeJf984bM"}
